ACCEPTThe new terminal cancellation theorem, virtual connector ledger, conditional beta-target lemma, and explicit stranded-demand obstruction are mathematically sound under the stated hypotheses. I found no substantive error requiring a change to the formulas or conclusions.There is one minor wording repair: “unique continuation” should mean “unique maximal continuation link set, up to interleaving the advances at the two ends.” The upper and lower advances can occur in different chronological orders. Their individual routes and final link set are forced.My acceptance concerns the written mathematics. I do not independently certify the reported checker runs, Lean execution, or axiom-audit output.1. Signed component conservation is correctLet  $E_{\mathrm{str}}$  be the matching consisting of the original strand edges, and let  $C$  be the matching of opposite-label terminal links. Retain edge identities in their multigraph union.Every terminal has exactly one strand incidence and at most one link incidence. Consequently, each connected component is an alternating path or an alternating cycle. A path’s endpoints are exactly its two terminals not incident to  $C$ .For a component  $K$ , let  $d(K)$  and  $b(K)$  count its original alpha and beta owners. Give TP terminals weight  $-1$  and BP terminals weight  $+1$ . Then
$$2\bigl(b(K)-d(K)\bigr)
=\sum_{v\in V(K)}w(v)
=\sum_{\substack{v\in V(K)\\v\text{ free}}}w(v).$$
The first equality counts every original strand owner once. The second holds because the linked vertices are partitioned into disjoint opposite-label pairs, each of weight zero. Thus
$$b(K)-d(K)=
\begin{cases}
-1,&K\text{ is a virtual TP--TP strand},\\
0,&K\text{ is a virtual mixed strand or a cycle},\\
1,&K\text{ is a virtual BP--BP strand}.
\end{cases}$$
This proves the signed conservation identity component by component, including components containing several original alpha and beta owners.Parallel two-edge cyclesIf a link joins the two terminals of one original mixed strand, the strand edge and link are distinct parallel edges. Both terminal degrees are two, so this is a legitimate alternating two-edge cycle. It has:One original mixed owner;No free terminals;Zero signed charge;No surviving virtual strand.It therefore satisfies both identities in equation (2). Geometric coincidence of the two edges does not produce another resource.Both ends of one beta ownerA beta owner contributes  $+1$  through its single strand edge, regardless of whether one or both terminals are linked. For example, an alpha–beta–alpha chain has total charge
$$-1+1-1=-1.$$
Its surviving virtual alpha still carries one full demand. The proof correctly prevents charging the two BP terminals as two credits.Number of surviving strandsThere are
$$2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)-2|C|$$
free terminals. Each path component contributes exactly two, and every cycle contributes none. Therefore
$$\alpha'+\beta'+\gamma'
=\alpha+\beta+\gamma-|C|.$$
No additional cycle term belongs in this equation. Combining the signed invariant with the original packet ledger gives exactly
$$S=L+\beta'-\alpha'.$$
Section 1 is correct.2. Virtual connectors preserve interval-side ownership without a vertical-mate assumptionThe crucial point is that connector capacity belongs to physical interval sides, and the argument identifying their possible users survives cancellation.Fix one side of one BB–TT interval. A direct port using that side must come from the immediately adjacent TP column in the same band. That column contains exactly one original endpoint, hence one original terminal vertex.That terminal:Can be free in at most one terminal-graph component;Can be used by at most one chosen virtual alpha strand;Receives only one chosen port.Hence a fixed interval side receives at most one connector incidence. Each interval has two sides, so its degree is at most two. A loop consumes both incidences.Nothing here requires the free TP terminal’s actual mate to be vertical. A free terminal inherited from an original mixed strand may have a horizontal actual mate. Its terminal identity and physical TP column still give exactly the ownership argument above.The boundary argument also remains valid. A marked interval meeting the first column has no available side beyond that boundary. A marked interval meeting a sealed final column has the analogous restriction. Thus every marked vertex has degree at most one and cannot lie on a connector cycle.The inherited distinctness of the  $B$  marked intervals is also sufficient: for even width, one odd-length BB–TT interval cannot contain both extreme columns; marks in different bands belong to different interval vertices.Consequently,
$$L-a'=h'_0+h'_1+h'_2,
\qquad
B=h'_1+2h'_2.$$
Using  $\alpha'=a'+u'$  gives
$$\begin{aligned}
S-B
&=L+\beta'-a'-u'-B\\
&=h'_0+\beta'-h'_2-u'.
\end{aligned}$$
Equation (3), including its “if and only if,” is therefore exact.No omitted cycle correctionThe two kinds of cycles disappear for different valid reasons:A terminal cancellation cycle has zero signed strand charge.A connector cycle has equal numbers of interval vertices and connector edges, so contributes zero to  $L-a'$ .Neither requires an additional debit in (3).The ownership statement also has the correct scope. Virtual beta resources and omitted virtual alpha demands are distinct terminal components. Unmarked and twice-marked connector paths are distinct connector components. A chosen virtual alpha is incorporated as an edge of one connector component rather than counted again as a separate resource or demand. None of this establishes physical disjointness of all underlying tile supports, and the note correctly says so.3. The beta-target hypothesis is sufficient, with exactly the stated limitationFor complete precision, write the hypothesis as
$$C=\bigl\{\{v,f(v)\}:v\in A\bigr\},$$
where  $A$  is the set of missing terminals of original alpha paths,  $f$  is the proved adjacent-terminal injection, and every  $f(v)$  belongs to an original beta path.This makes explicit that  $C$  consists exactly of those injection links, with no additional links involving mixed owners. That is the natural reading of the current text.Under this hypothesis:Every original alpha terminal without a port is linked and therefore cannot remain free.No original mixed owner is touched: its TP terminal is not in  $A$ , and its BP terminal is excluded by the beta-target condition.Any affected component contains only original alpha and beta owners.Every free TP terminal of such a component must therefore be an original alpha terminal.Since it remains free, it was not missing and has an original BB port.Untouched original alpha strands also have both ports; otherwise one of their terminals would have belonged to  $A$  and been linked. Untouched mixed strands remain mixed.Thus every virtual alpha is attachable, and choosing all of them gives
$$u'=0.$$
This argument is sound.However, it does not establish  $h'_2=0$ . Connecting two ported terminals can still join boundary-marked components. The note correctly imposes the independent condition  $h'_2=0$ , or more generally
$$h'_2\le h'_0+\beta'.$$
Complete freezing is used to obtain the original injection. Once the exact injection and beta-target property are assumed, the port conclusion itself is structural.The phrase “essential to this argument” is appropriately limited. Beta targets are not necessary for port exposure in every individual configuration. They are a sufficient condition that excludes migration onto unported mixed-owner TP terminals. The obstruction family proves that one cannot simply delete this condition and retain the conclusion.The outside-ledger corollary is also correct as a conditional substitution. From
$$\text{global margin}
=\sum_J S_J+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}-2N_{\rm out}$$
and  $S_J\ge B_J$ , the stated inequality
$$q+2N_{\rm out}
\le \sum_J B_J+D_{\rm out}+R_{\rm out}$$
implies nonnegative global margin. Physical packet disjointness and complete original receiver closure remain separate hypotheses. Terminal cancellation does not prove them, and the note does not claim otherwise.4. Thus feasibility is directly visible from the coordinate lists.The counts are

At each step, the first named endpoint has exactly one remaining endpoint neighbor. This exhausts  $P$ , so the displayed actual matching is unique for every permitted  $W,H$ .Complete freezing also has a uniform direct proofThe supplied small certificate is valid, but the all-parameter claim can additionally be checked without relying on its finite instances.Call an endpoint retained once its actual mate has frozen. Use

along with  $U_c,L_c$  above. The following serial schedule supplies two distinct nonmate witnesses at every event:Freeze the four selected-supported tips

When  $c\le H$ , next freeze  $U_{c+1}$  using retained  $U_c,L_{c+1}$ .The actual mate of every retained witness occurs strictly earlier in this schedule. It covers all  $2(W+H)$  endpoints. This independently confirms complete freezing uniformly in both parameters.For the supplied  $W=6,H=4$  certificate, every listed event also checks directly. The stranded-demand and continuation claims have the correct scopeUsing TP, BP and BT as unordered column types, the two displayed row patterns are correct. The selected corner lies above the endpoint in the upper terminal band and below it in the lower terminal band; this reversal does not affect the type or port arguments.At the original alpha terminals, the left neighbor is selected and the only horizontal BP neighbor is at column  $4$ . Thus the first injection is forced:
$$(5,3)\longleftrightarrow(5,4),
\qquad

These BP terminals belong to different original mixed owners. Their other terminals are  $(5,5)$  and  $(R,5)$ , both unported. The resulting component contains one alpha and two mixed owners, so it has charge  $-1$  and remains a virtual alpha. The inventory

is correct.Continuing while retaining previous linksAt each new free terminal, the BP immediately behind it has already been used. Advancing through an unused BP therefore forces the next displayed link.The maximal link set consists of the two upper links and the  $H/2$  lower links, terminating at
$$(5,7),\qquad (R,H+3).$$
Both final terminals remain unported. The maximal continuation has
$$|C|=2+\frac H2,\qquad
\alpha'=1,\qquad
\beta'=0,\qquad
\gamma'=\frac H2-1.$$
This agrees with the supplied smallest example.As noted at the outset, the link set is unique under this rule, but the chronological ordering of upper and lower advances is not. That is the only repair needed to the uniqueness wording.Hall deficiency and reassignmentThe horizontal neighbor counts are exact:Terminal rowMissing TP terminalsAll available horizontal BP neighbors $5$  $3$  $2$  $R$  $H/2+1$  $H/2$ Thus no matching of horizontal terminal links can cover every missing TP in either row.The note correctly limits what this pigeonhole argument proves. Hall deficiency alone does not generally show that the unmatched TP terminal belongs to a virtual alpha rather than a virtual mixed strand. It rules out a strategy requiring all missing TP terminals to be covered.For this specific family, a stronger conclusion is available from the signed invariant and row geometry:Every mixed owner in row  $5$  stays entirely in that row.Every mixed owner in row  $R$  stays entirely in that row.The sole original alpha is the only owner connecting those two rows.Other mixed owners lie in row  $R-1$ , inaccessible from those rows by horizontal terminal links.There are no beta owners.Therefore, under any matching of horizontal terminal links, the component containing the original alpha has charge  $-1$ . The family refutes the automatic rule, not the target inequalityFor the first injection and the maximal continuation, the only virtual alpha is unported, so no direct connector is added. Every interval vertex is isolated in the connector graph. Since  $L=S+1$ ,
$$h'_1=B,\qquad
h'_0=S+1-B,\qquad
h'_2=0,\qquad
u'=1,\qquad
\beta'=0.$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}
h'_0+\beta'-h'_2-u'
&=S-B\\
&=WH+4W+10H+51\\
&>0.
\end{aligned}$$
At  $W=6,H=4$ , this gives
$$S=157,\qquad B=18,\qquad h'_0=140,\qquad S-B=139.$$
The family therefore refutes:Automatic exposure of a direct BB port after cancellation;Counting every encountered BP terminal as one credit;Reapplication of the original-alpha injection theorem to arbitrary virtual-alpha endpoints.It does not refute  $S\ge B$ . The residual unit debit remains present and is outweighed by actual interval reserves. The note keeps that distinction clear.Separated stacking preserves the argument: the translated occupied cores have no new occupied adjacencies, their certificates remain valid, and each original alpha retains its own stranded component.7. $$S-B=h'_0+\beta'$$
and nonnegativity. It does not itself encode the beta-target hypothesis or prove that the omitted and twice-marked terms vanish.The written scope statement is therefore appropriate. The theorem names should continue to be interpreted together with their actual hypotheses, not as a claim that the geometric adapter has been formalized.8. One focused next step: selected-cap access to interval resourcesA promising next step is to extend the connector adapter by one precisely owned local access pattern:
$$\boxed{\mathrm{TP}\;-\;\mathrm{BT}\;-\;\mathrm{BB}}$$
where the BT column’s selection lies in the terminal’s physical row, and all three columns lie in the same band. Call this selected-cap access, distinguishing it from the existing immediately adjacent BB port.The ownership lemma has a short proof. Fix one interval side:If the immediately external column is TP, that side can support ordinary direct access.If it is BT, that side can support selected-cap access from the next column.These cases are mutually exclusive.In the BT case, the selected corner specifies the terminal row, and the next TP column contains only one original terminal.Thus a fixed interval side still has at most one possible terminal user. With one chosen access per free terminal, interval degree remains at most two and marked-boundary degree remains at most one. The same path/cycle Euler ledger applies. The intervening selection contributes no new credit.This access is explicit in the present obstruction after maximal continuation:
$$(5,7)\longrightarrow \mathrm{BT}_8
\longrightarrow \mathrm{BB}_9$$
in band  $(4,5)$ , and
$$(R,H+3)\longrightarrow \mathrm{BT}_{H+4}
\longrightarrow \mathrm{BB}_{H+5}$$
in band  $(R,R+1)$ .The two BB intervals are distinct, unmarked, and isolated. Connecting them through the sole virtual alpha replaces two isolated unmarked components by one unmarked path. Accordingly,
$$a'\mapsto a'+1,\qquad
u'\mapsto u'-1,\qquad
h'_0\mapsto h'_0-1.$$
The ledger is preserved exactly: the demand is paid by consuming one unit of actual interval reserve. For this family, the extended connector graph has
$$u'=0,\qquad h'_2=0,\qquad \beta'=0,\qquad h'_0=S-B.$$
This gives a concrete interval-resource payment for the whole obstruction family and its separated stacks. The next bounded lemma should establish this direct-or-selected-cap ownership adapter explicitly. A general compensation theorem would still need to prove sufficient access or allocation for arbitrary residual demands and control twice-marked paths; neither follows merely from introducing the additional access pattern.
